## Purpose

Brings into `m31-pp-opt` the remaining changes the MiniMax-M3.1 PP prefill benchmark ran with, so the branch reproduces it. Three commits on top of the branch head (`c905d49982`):

1. **Pair KV regions by layer for every transfer**: #63416 as one commit (@Dao007forever, with @NickLucche).
2. **Pull KV from pipeline-parallel prefill stages**: #64397, stacked on #63416. Both stay open against `main` for review; this branch only carries them.
3. **Reserve the Q8KV4 prefill workspace on every SM10x GPU** (new). The Q8KV4 prefill split workspace was reserved only on Rubin (SM107). On B200/B300 the prefill allocated its split partials on every step, about 8 GiB at 32K tokens, outside memory profiling. So PP2 with `--gpu-memory-utilization 0.9` ran out of memory on its first long prefill:
   ```
   torch.OutOfMemoryError: CUDA out of memory. Tried to allocate 8.00 GiB. GPU 1 has a total capacity of 267.68 GiB of which 458.25 MiB is free.
   ```
   This commit reserves the workspace once, for the largest batch, on the whole SM10x family.

## Test Plan

- NIXL unit tests:
  ```bash
  pytest tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_nixl_desc_geometry.py \
         tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_nixl_connector_hma.py \
         tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_nixl_push_connector.py
  ```
- The full PP prefill benchmark, run with this branch on `vllm/vllm-openai:cu134-nightly-335dd77b0`. The setup was one 8-GPU HGX B300 node and MiniMax-M3.1-Flash with the NVFP4 KV cache. TP2, DEP2 and PP2 were each screened, swept and repeated over three seeds, all at `--gpu-memory-utilization 0.9`.

## Test Result

- NIXL: the 12 files of commits 1-2 are byte-identical to #64397's head. On a CPU-only machine, the failure set of the tests above is identical to #64397's head; the failures come from the missing CUDA/NIXL environment.
- Workspace: without commit 3, PP2 with the CuTe DSL MoE ran out of memory on the first long prefill at 0.9. With it, every PP2 config ran screening, sweeps and finals at 0.9 with no out-of-memory error.
- Accuracy: GSM8K (all 1,319 questions) is 0.9613 for PP2's final config, against 0.9568 for the TP2 reference. Every config also matched the reference's first token on 64 long prompts (top-1 agreement 1.0).

AI assistance: commits 1-2 were assembled with Claude Code from the existing PRs; commit 3 and the benchmark runs were done with Claude Code and reviewed by the submitter.

@@ -194,31 +194,40 @@ accounting code is unchanged.
 
 ## Pipeline parallelism and hybrid KV caches
 
-The pull connector requires the local and remote workers to expose a
-congruent list of KV regions — region *i* here corresponds to region
-*i* there. That assumption breaks under pipeline parallelism (PP)
-combined with a hybrid (HMA) KV layout:
+A peer's KV regions do not line up with the local ones by index under
+pipeline parallelism (PP) or a hybrid (HMA) KV layout:
 
 * a PP-sharded prefiller (**P**) holds only a slice of the model's
   layers while the `PP=1` decoder (**D**) holds them all, so region
   counts differ;
-* with HMA, several layer names are pooled into one region and the layer
-  that represents a pooled region can differ between P and D.
-
-`NixlPushConnector` handles this for PP-sharded producers by routing
-**by layer name** instead of by region index. Each
-worker advertises which layer names back each of its NIXL regions in the
-handshake metadata (`NixlAgentMetadata.region_members`). A producer that
-needs layer routing derives its transfer layer order once, when it
-registers its KV caches, and every transfer it issues uses that order.
-`add_remote_agent` then selects exactly the remote regions this stage
-owns and reorders them to match, so both sides stay paired regardless of
-how each remote rank happens to order its metadata.
-
-Addresses, block lengths, strides, and per-region capacities follow the same
-layer order. Descriptor offsets use each layer's region capacity, so P and
-D need not allocate the same number of blocks. Physical allocations are still
-registered once, even when multiple layers share them.
+* with HMA, layers of several cache groups can share one region, and
+  which layers share a region can differ between P and D.
+
+Both connectors therefore pair regions **by layer**, for every peer. Each
+worker advertises which layers back each of its NIXL regions in the
+handshake metadata (`NixlAgentMetadata.region_members`). On the
+handshake, `_pair_regions` looks each layer up on both sides and records
+one pair (remote region, local region, cache group) per layer,
+deduplicated; a layer registered as two regions (K and V apart) pairs
+them in order. The remote descriptor list keeps only the remote regions
+that pair, and a transfer reads or writes each pair at its cache group's
+blocks. A region shared by several groups thus transfers once per group
+it holds a layer of, from one descriptor list.
+
